capabilities.statement: a pane is only ever created from a type the registry declares
capabilities.mechanism: `PaneTypes.ALL` is the closed table every surface reads — menu, palette, sidebar, restore and the control socket — and `sanitize_tile` drops a saved tile whose type it does not carry
capabilities.row: Tiling grid layout

capabilities.statement: a new pane halves the largest tile and a closed pane returns its rectangle to the grid
capabilities.mechanism: `_split_for` halves the largest tile on the caller's side or the axis its aspect prefers; on detach an exact neighbour absorbs the freed rect, else one edge group that spans it
capabilities.row: Tiling grid layout

capabilities.statement: closing a pane asks once for the running work the whole action would stop
capabilities.mechanism: every destruction path goes through `PaneBody.request_close`; `_ask_running_then` aggregates `has_running_work` for the set and names the workspace and panes in one dialog
capabilities.row: Reset or closing a pane asks before killing running work

capabilities.statement: two panes exchange rectangles, and a pane's type can be replaced without losing its id
capabilities.mechanism: the tile geometry is swapped in place and both wrappers re-lay out; a type change is a separate named action that rebuilds the body through `_swap_pane` and keeps the attachment id
capabilities.row: Pane position and type swapping

capabilities.statement: a pane can be hidden while its child process keeps running, and restored with the keyboard back in it
capabilities.mechanism: `toggle_pane_minimize` flips the wrapper's visibility only; a restore returns focus to the pane through `_return_focus_to_body`, and a minimize deliberately leaves nothing focused
capabilities.row: Pane chrome: distinct icons, a compact action menu, padding and consistent empty states

capabilities.statement: dragging a divider moves the shared edge a grid unit at a time, and the release commits what the preview showed
capabilities.mechanism: `TileDrag` snapshots the line's geometry at the press, previews in whole grid units, and replays the same sequence on release; the workspace keeps the axis resize cursor for the whole drag
capabilities.row: Resizing a pane is smooth: the resize cursor always shows, no gray band while dragging, no hop on release

capabilities.statement: a workspace switch changes which grid is drawn, not what is running
capabilities.mechanism: each workspace owns a grid and a tile manager over one live pane set; the inactive grids are hidden and their process mode disabled, so a hidden pane keeps its child and its grid alive
capabilities.row: Workspace switching

capabilities.statement: workspace names, directories, profiles and each grid's tiles survive a restart
capabilities.mechanism: `_gather_tiles` serializes through the same sanitizer a restore runs, and the store is written on quit and on every switch; an empty grid is saved as empty and restores empty
capabilities.row: Session auto-save

capabilities.statement: a restore names the settings, environment and panes it refused instead of dropping them silently
capabilities.mechanism: `sanitize_tile` reports each dropped key and `_restore_into` raises one toast per class — unsupported setting, file-supplied environment, pane ceiling — naming the panes and where to fix it

capabilities.statement: one theme built from the tokens is the only theme the app runs on, rebuilt when the palette switches
capabilities.mechanism: `UiTheme.build` reads the active palette and `UiTokens` at build time and is set on the workspace root; a switch rebuilds it there, so every pane, overlay, popup and dialog inherits one copy
capabilities.row: Shared theme, type scale, colour tokens and UI scale

capabilities.statement: the chrome has a complete dark set and a complete light set, and no surface caches a colour
capabilities.mechanism: both tables carry the same keys, a missing one fails the unit test, and every widget reads `UiPalette.active()` at draw time, because a cached value keeps the mode it was built under
capabilities.row: The app chrome has a light theme, and it follows the system

capabilities.statement: sizes, spacing and radii come from a named scale, and a UI scale is capped so the layout keeps its floor
capabilities.mechanism: the `FS_*`, `SPACE_*` and `RADIUS` constants replace literals; `ui_scale_ceiling` caps the applied factor so window pixels divided by scale never fall under `MIN_LAYOUT`, and an unmeasurable window is not capped
capabilities.row: Shared theme, type scale, colour tokens and UI scale

capabilities.statement: every text-on-surface pair is graded against a minimum ratio in both palettes
capabilities.mechanism: `CONTRAST_PAIRS` lists each pair with its floor and the unit test grades them with `UiTokens.contrast_ratio`, the same alpha-composited maths a measurement quotes
capabilities.row: Shared theme, type scale, colour tokens and UI scale

capabilities.statement: a pane is one named region that says which pane it is and what kind
capabilities.mechanism: `refresh_accessibility_name` joins the label and the display name, and an icon button's glyph is drawn in a child label so a private-use codepoint never becomes the exposed name

capabilities.statement: a custom-drawn pane's visible text and a one-line change are both readable through the accessible tree
capabilities.mechanism: `A11y.publish` replaces a content node under the tile's title bar when the text changes and a polite live node carries announcements; role and value are written only from the control's own accessibility update
capabilities.row: A restored terminal publishes no text to the AT-SPI tree

capabilities.statement: the keyboard enters each surface at a named control, moves in one explicit ring and draws an accent ring on the focused stop
capabilities.mechanism: `PaneBody.keyboard_entry` and `WindowChrome.focus_controls` name the entry, `KeyboardFocus.ring` writes the wrapping order, and the theme's focus stylebox is a 1 px accent border
capabilities.row: Keyboard focus is explicit and does not leak

capabilities.statement: a typed query ranks label prefixes first, then label substrings, then command and keyword hits
capabilities.mechanism: `PaletteModel.filter` scans in three tiers and keeps the model's own order inside a tier, so the cursor's first row after a keystroke is predictable and a name never reorders the list
capabilities.row: Command palette: population, selection and honest entries

capabilities.statement: the shortcut list is read from the binding registry, so a chord cannot drift from the key that runs it
capabilities.mechanism: `ShortcutCatalog` groups name actions and `rows` takes the registry reader; an action with no chord is omitted, and the new-pane group is built from the pane registry

capabilities.statement: an empty workspace teaches every binding with a keycap demo and a launch action
capabilities.mechanism: `ShortcutGuide` renders the catalog as grouped cards, cycles the spawn chords read from the registry through a keycap, and is shown exactly when the active workspace has no tiles
capabilities.row: The empty workspace teaches every shortcut, with a living keycap

capabilities.statement: the bottom bar names the focused pane and carries frame rate, clock and version
capabilities.mechanism: two labels: the left is the pane's icon, label and type resolved from the focus owner, the right joins the live readouts, and a capture can freeze them for a repeatable image

capabilities.statement: the sidebar lists workspaces, profiles and panes as foldable sections that scroll as one column
capabilities.mechanism: each section is a header plus a list capped at five measured rows, the whole column scrolls when the window is shorter, and a pane row mutates in place and opens the same menu as the pane's title bar
capabilities.row: The sidebar's three sections cannot be folded

capabilities.statement: window mode, fullscreen and window position persist, and the maximize control says what pressing it will do
capabilities.mechanism: `apply_mode` puts the configured mode on the window and swaps the control's glyph and name from the setting; position is saved and restored only in a windowed mode, and a fullscreen toggle returns to borderless windowed
capabilities.row: Window controls never swap maximize/restore

capabilities.statement: messages show one at a time, each for its own lifetime, with a bounded backlog
capabilities.mechanism: the visible toast owns its tween and starts the next when it ends; the queue is capped at eight and drops the oldest, so a caller in a loop cannot grow it
capabilities.row: The toast queue never queues

capabilities.statement: a scrolling pane offers a jump to its start and its end, each visible only while that direction has content
capabilities.mechanism: `ScrollHints` binds to a scrollbar, a tree or a pane's own offset and shows each chevron from its own predicate, so a body that fits its viewport shows neither
capabilities.row: Every scrolling pane carries the same two scroll chevrons

capabilities.statement: an agent state is told apart by its silhouette rather than its colour, and its words are its accessible name
capabilities.mechanism: four shapes, one per state, with a painted ring for working because a thin glyph arc faded at badge size; the tooltip and exposed name are the state's words, never a codepoint
capabilities.row: The `working` badge is a thin arc that reads as a dim dot at 12 px

capabilities.statement: a created, closed or swapped pane moves between its rectangles instead of appearing and vanishing in one frame
capabilities.mechanism: no motion layer exists: `_apply_layout` writes every rect in one pass, so a new pane appears fully formed, a closed one vanishes and a swap teleports both bodies
capabilities.row: Panes animate when they are created, destroyed or swapped

capabilities.statement: motion can be turned down without changing what the interface does
capabilities.mechanism: no motion setting exists; the badge's ring and the guide's keycap animate on a wall clock and only the capture harness can pin them
capabilities.row: Panes animate when they are created, destroyed or swapped

capabilities.statement: the window can be made translucent and the terminal can keep a padding inset without lying about its grid
capabilities.mechanism: neither setting exists: text sits flush against the pane edge and the grid fills the pane's whole rect
capabilities.row: Window fit: opacity and inner padding

capabilities.statement: a user can change a shortcut binding
capabilities.mechanism: chords are registered once and the catalog reads them back, but nothing writes a binding from user input
capabilities.row: Keybindings are configurable

capabilities.statement: a colour scheme can be imported from another terminal's format, and a light and dark pair can follow the system
capabilities.mechanism: only three schemes ship and no importer exists; the chrome's dark and light pair is a user choice rather than a reading of the system state
capabilities.row: Colour schemes: import, and light mode that follows the system

capabilities.statement: terminal visual effects come only from a closed built-in table and are off by default
capabilities.mechanism: `UiEffects` holds the two ambient `preload` shader paths and the Off/Subtle/Full intensity; `PaneEffects` paints the ground through one dedicated effect layer and the row runs at the default background are skipped under it, so text, selection and coloured cells stay opaque
capabilities.row: Dynamic Shaders

capabilities.statement: a concept event can cue the pane that fired it, rate-limited and display-only
capabilities.mechanism: `UiEffects.REACTIVE` is the closed cue table with one fixed palette tone per cue; the concept drain calls `_flash_concept`, and `PaneEffects` enforces 334 ms per pane, skips hidden panes and draws a tint, a border pulse or a fixed 48-particle burst from a pool allocated once
capabilities.row: Reactive Environments
